title: Forward Engine Mount Link Bushing — Inspection
abstract: Inspection of the forward engine mount link bushings for liner degradation and radial play, including the heat shield condition check that indicates whether the bushing has been running above its design temperature.

sections.purpose: To inspect the forward engine mount link bushings for liner degradation and radial play and to assess the heat shield condition that drives it.
sections.job_setup_note: The engine must have been shut down for at least four hours and the pylon area must be cool enough to work in. The fan cowl and the pylon access panels must be open. The engine must be supported on the mount jack before any measurement is taken with the link loaded. Two persons are needed and a third is required if the link is to be removed following a finding.
sections.procedure: WARNING: DO NOT WORK AT THE FORWARD MOUNT UNTIL THE ENGINE HAS BEEN SHUT DOWN FOR AT LEAST FOUR HOURS. THE PYLON STRUCTURE RETAINS HEAT LONG AFTER THE COWL IS COOL. Put the safety barriers in position and open the fan cowl and the pylon access panels. Put the engine mount jack in position and take the weight. Clean the link ends and the bushing bores. Examine the heat shield CAD50991-63 for discolouration, for distortion and for loss of the coating, and photograph any finding where the operator procedure allows it. Examine each link bushing liner for extrusion at the ends, for cracking and for a change of colour from tan to dark brown, which indicates over-temperature. CAUTION: A LINER THAT HAS DARKENED MUST BE TREATED AS A FINDING EVEN IF THE PLAY IS INSIDE LIMITS. THE MATERIAL DEGRADES BEFORE THE PLAY OPENS UP. Measure the radial play at each bushing with the dial gauge, with the engine weight on the jack and then with the weight on the mount, and record both values. Examine the shroud D7120114517025 and the nozzle kit D7120115408026 for fretting at the contact faces. Make sure that the tension bolts AES840808-93 and the titanium bolts LN569360-2A are correctly torqued and that the witness marks are aligned. Compare the recorded play with the limits.
sections.close_out: Remove the engine mount jack. Make sure that no tool or hardware remains in the pylon. Close the pylon access panels and the fan cowl. Remove the safety barriers. Record the heat shield condition, the liner condition at each bushing, both radial play readings and the torque witness state. Refer any liner discolouration or any play outside limits to the engineering department before the next flight.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The interval extends on aircraft carrying the deeper heat shield.

safety_precautions: Do not work at the forward mount until the engine has been shut down for at least four hours.
Support the engine on the mount jack before any loaded measurement.
Put the safety barriers in position.
